solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cloth covering prostrate bloke leaving hospital

indicators.note: to leave a place is to go out of it, so the bloke goes out of the hospital and H drops from CHAP

parts.note: chap = bloke; H = hospital, as on road signs, is taken out

explanation.surface: A cloth is draped over a man lying flat as he is discharged from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cloth covering" reads like a sheet over a patient, but it is the definition: a covering for the head made of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by material and use: this traditional British working man's hat is a soft cloth covering for the head.

clue.text: Complicated foxtrot lazily interrupted by duke

parts.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

explanation.surface: A foxtrot danced half-heartedly gets messy when a duke cuts in.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballroom picture makes "foxtrot" a dance, but here it is just the radio code word for F.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a task full of small awkward steps is complicated to do.

clue.text: Animal is unable to stand without beginning to collapse

indicators.note: the phrase must do without the letter named next, so that letter is removed
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: can't bear = is unable to stand (tolerate)
first letter of collapse, which is taken away

explanation.surface: An animal too weak to stand is about to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stand" looks physical in the surface, but the wordplay wants 'tolerate'. The antbear is better known as the aardvark.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the aardvark, also called the antbear, is an animal.

clue.text: Briefly had sheep rearing a pony

indicators.note: said briefly, cut short, so CONNED loses its last letter
a rearing animal rises up on its hind legs; in a down clue that turns the word bottom to top

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, turned upward

explanation.surface: Someone briefly kept sheep that raised a pony.
explanation.walkthrough: "Had" as in 'I've been had' means tricked. The "a" is used in the wordplay and reappears in the definition, a common Times economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Connemara is a hardy pony breed from the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Head of Science spied their new lab equipment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
something new has been made over, so the letters come out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The head of the science department sees the lab's shiny new kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits inside the scene it describes, so only the awkward "spied their" gives the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: these shallow lidded dishes for growing cultures are standard lab equipment.

clue.text: Star worker in Spain will be retiring

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw, go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: será is Spanish for 'will be'; it then turns round

explanation.surface: A star employee in Spain is about to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: "Star worker" reads as one phrase, but the break comes after "Star". "In Spain" tells you to use the Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Antares is the bright red star at the heart of Scorpius.

clue.text: Cockney's shock appearance

definitions.meaning: a shock is a thick mop of hair, said without its H

indicators.note: a Cockney famously drops the H at the start of a word, so this is how a Cockney says the word for a shock

definitions.meaning: the look or manner someone gives off

explanation.surface: Something about how a Cockney looks gives you a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: "Shock" means a thick mass of hair, not a fright. Cockneys, the working-class Londoners of the East End, drop their Hs: 'air for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a dropped-H hair, and the air someone has, their outward appearance or manner.

clue.text: Something symbolic in anthem swapping first and last parts

indicators.note: to swap is to exchange places, so the first and last letters trade ends

parts.note: a motet is a short choral anthem; its outer letters M and T change places

explanation.surface: A symbolic moment in an anthem where the opening and closing verses are sung the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: "Parts" suggests sections of music, but here each part is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a totem is an emblem standing for a clan or group, something symbolic.

clue.text: Composer somewhat cross initially

indicators.note: somewhat means to some degree, so only some of the letters that follow are used

parts.note: the answer runs from the second letter of cross into the first four of initially

explanation.surface: A composer who started out a bit grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Initially" tempts you to take first letters; it is only fodder: c(ROSS INI)tially.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Gioachino Rossini, who wrote The Barber of Seville, was an Italian composer.

clue.text: Tooth broken by penny sweet is fixed

indicators.note: something broken is split open

parts.note: rock is a hard stick of candy sold at British seaside resorts

explanation.surface: A tooth snaps on a hard penny sweet and has to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The dentist story makes "Tooth" a molar; it is a tooth on a cog wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical sense: each of the projections on a wheel that engage a chain is a tooth.

clue.text: Revolutionary turned, checking on cause of explosion

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word runs backwards
to check is to hold back or restrain, so the reversed word holds ON inside it

parts.note: as printed, held in the middle of the reversed word

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who changed sides checks up on what set off a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: "Revolutionary" looks like the usual RED or CHE, but here it is the reversal instruction for "turned".
explanation.definitionFit: A functional description: the small charge that sets off the main explosive is the cause of the explosion.

clue.text: Stunner posed on the counter with hesitant expression

indicators.note: counter means contrary, running the opposite way, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: sat, as for a portrait, then turned round

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman poses on a shop counter looking unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stunner" reads as a beauty; it is the stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful sense: the brand of electric stun gun is literally something that stuns.

clue.text: Port for one tucking into pork pie

parts.note: pork pie = lie, Cockney rhyming slang (also shortened to porky)

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a pork pie with a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: "Port" looks like the drink; it is a river port. In Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie, or porky, is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Belgian city on the Meuse is a major inland river port.

clue.text: Not sleeping at home regularly once man is fooling around

indicators.note: letters that fool around will not keep still, so they are rearranged
at regular intervals, so every other letter: O and C from once

parts.note: o-n-c-e, 1st and 3rd letters, into the anagram

explanation.surface: A man lies awake at night because his partner is out fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: The story of a spouse lying awake hides a three-step build, and "regularly" works on "once" alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective sense: an insomniac night or person is one not sleeping.

clue.text: Led race to secure region occupied by husband and daughter

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast
an occupied place has someone living in it

parts.note: d = daughter, placed after the region

explanation.surface: A man led the race to capture a territory his husband and daughter had moved into.
explanation.walkthrough: The containers are loose: the husband goes inside the region, but the daughter simply follows it, both still within the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: to spearhead a campaign is to go at its front, to lead it.

clue.text: Business offering protection perhaps involved in more disgrace

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A security firm finds itself in deeper scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: "Protection" reads as security; the definition means the protection racket, where gangsters charge to leave you alone. "In" belongs to the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': selling 'protection' is a classic racket of gangsters, so a business of that kind.

clue.text: Officer close to despondency over Conservative restriction on reproduction

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of despondency
in a down clue one piece written over another comes first

parts.note: the right = the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: A despairing officer on a Tory birth-control policy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Reproduction" suggests babies; it means copying a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal sense: this right limits who may copy, i.e. reproduce, a creative work.

clue.text: I'm sorry cast made porn

indicators.note: metal that is cast is moulded into a new shape, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: An apology from actors who made a blue film.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cast" looks like the actors in the film; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrases are everyday ways of apologising.

clue.text: Someone whose treatment might incense their workplace

definitions.text: Someone whose treatment might incense their workplace

parts.note: the surface pushes 'the way someone treats their colleagues'; the setter means a therapeutic treatment given to clients
the surface pushes in-CENSE, to enrage; the setter means IN-cense, to fill the room with fragrant scent

explanation.surface: A worker whose way of treating people makes the office furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Read incense as the verb 'anger' and you want a bad boss; stress the first syllable and it means perfuming the room with burning scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a practitioner treating clients with scented oils fills the treatment room with fragrance, as incense would.

clue.text: Very large African nation adopting name of Turkish empire

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in as one's own

explanation.surface: A huge African country takes on the name of the Ottoman Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Osman, founder of the Ottoman dynasty; Ottoman is the same name in another form.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjectival synonym: this is the Turkish form of Ottoman, meaning belonging to that empire.

clue.text: Self-satisfied delight, finishing early run

indicators.note: a word that finishes early stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: glee = delight, less its last letter

explanation.surface: A smug runner gloats after finishing a race ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: "Run" looks like a jog; it means to run goods, as in gun-running.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade sense: to run contraband past customs is to bring it in illegally.

clue.text: Sage perhaps injecting drug over years as a result of this

indicators.note: to inject is to put something inside
in a down clue one piece written over another comes first

explanation.surface: A wise old man has been injecting drugs for years as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sage" reads as a wise man; "perhaps" marks it as an example of the answer's first chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: the legal word means by means of this, so as a result of this.

clue.text: Mostly try and measure diamonds from the east in cup

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so ESSAY loses its last letter
an across clue is read west to east, so from the east means right to left

parts.note: essay = try (an attempt), less its last letter
to time = to measure with a clock

explanation.surface: Someone tries to weigh diamonds from the Orient in a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: "Try" is essay in its old sense of an attempt, not test. The reversal covers all three pieces at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this small coffee cup, French for half-cup, is a cup.

clue.text: Student is trade union supporter of course

parts.note: a golf tee holds up the ball on the course

explanation.surface: A student is, naturally, a union supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: "Of course" reads as 'naturally'; it is a golf course, and the tee supports the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: one taught by a tutor is a student.

clue.text: Course about nursing available

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, as a baby

parts.note: out = on sale, available, as a new book is

explanation.surface: A course on nursing is now on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a training course; it is a course as in a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the course taken between places is the way you go.

clue.text: New start, rejecting second instrumental group

indicators.note: to reject is to throw out, so ONSET throws out the letter for second

parts.note: onset = start; s = second is removed

explanation.surface: A band makes a fresh start after dropping its second player.
explanation.walkthrough: "New start" looks like a single phrase; "New" gives one letter and "start" the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: an ensemble of nine players is one kind of instrumental group.

clue.text: On vacation, people expected to ring back golf teacher

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it
a vacated place is emptied, so people loses everything but its outer letters

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers are due to phone a golf instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ring back" reads as returning a call, but "to ring" is the container and "back" is a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym, usually with a hint of pedantry: a schoolmaster is a teacher.

clue.text: Very old Scotsman forgets about depression

indicators.note: whatever is forgotten is left out

parts.note: the Picts lived in ancient Scotland
c = circa, about, as on dates; this is dropped

explanation.surface: An elderly Scot's memory lapses leave him feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: "Depression" reads as low spirits; it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A physical sense: a hole sunk into the ground is a depression in it.

clue.text: Famous English setter's not losing heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so NOT loses its central O

parts.note: the setter's, from the setter's point of view

explanation.surface: A well-known English setter keeps his spirits up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Setter" could be a dog; in crosswords it is the compiler, so the setter's = mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: someone distinguished and well known in their field is famous.

clue.text: Indecisive article in journal's replaced with another

indicators.note: to replace one thing with another is to take it out and put the other in its place

parts.note: the definite article, put in where A was

explanation.surface: A wishy-washy piece in a magazine has been swapped for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: "Article" looks like a piece of writing, which suits "journal"; here it is the grammar word, a or the.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who dithers keeps wavering, unable to decide.
